# HTraceView

> Expandable execution steps with status, durations and nested details.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HTraceView` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-trace-view>`.
- Constructor: `HearthTraceViewElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Developer.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HTraceView.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Read-only execution steps with native details disclosures. duration is displayed in milliseconds. expanded is controlled through update:expanded; defaultExpanded initializes local state. Details are escaped plain text. Default node/depth limits are 300/8; cycles and truncated branches are disclosed. Streaming updates are application-owned and do not generate per-frame live announcements.

## Public API

items: TraceItem[] · label: string · expanded, defaultExpanded: string[] · maxNodes, maxDepth: number

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    items: TraceItem[];
    label: string;
    expanded?: string[];
    defaultExpanded?: string[];
    maxNodes?: number;
    maxDepth?: number;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ items: () => [], defaultExpanded: () => [], maxNodes: 300, maxDepth: 8 }
```

### Events

update:expanded(string[])

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:expanded": [
        ids: string[]
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base

Use `hearth-trace-view::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface TraceItem {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    status?: RunStatus;
    duration?: number;
    description?: string;
    details?: string;
    children?: TraceItem[];
}

export type RunStatus = "pending" | "running" | "success" | "error" | "skipped";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HTraceView } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HTraceView label="Agent execution" :default-expanded="['run']" :items="[{id:'run',label:'Investigate',status:'running',children:[{id:'search',label:'Search repository',status:'success',duration:240,details:'Found 8 matching files.'},{id:'read',label:'Read source',status:'running'}]}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-trace-view');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Agent execution",
  "defaultExpanded": [
    "run"
  ],
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "run",
      "label": "Investigate",
      "status": "running",
      "children": [
        {
          "id": "search",
          "label": "Search repository",
          "status": "success",
          "duration": 240,
          "details": "Found 8 matching files."
        },
        {
          "id": "read",
          "label": "Read source",
          "status": "running"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('update:expanded', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
